title: AlphaFlow: Understanding and Improving MeanFlow Models
claim: Under the same seeds and sampling budget, our objective yields sharper, more coherent samples than the baseline, in both one-step and two-step generation.
layout: 4 stacked rows of 8 images; baseline vs ours for 1-step (top pair) and 2-step (bottom pair); green/red frames mark better/worse samples
description: A dense grid of 4 rows by 8 columns of generated ImageNet-style photos: parrots, an axolotl, a stork on a nest, a cockatoo, a hillside, a sea turtle, a robin, and a coastal seascape. Rows alternate between the baseline and the proposed method, with the same seeds and classes across rows. The upper pair is 1-step sampling and the lower pair is 2-step sampling. Several images in the proposed-method rows have green borders where they are clearly better, with one red border where they are worse. The baseline rows show blurrier, less detailed, or distorted samples, such as a smeared axolotl or a pink cast. The proposed rows show crisper textures and more saturated colors. The eye goes first to the colorful images and the green and red frames.

abstract: MeanFlow has recently emerged as a powerful framework for few-step generative modeling trained from scratch, but its success is not yet fully understood. In this work, we show that the MeanFlow objective naturally decomposes into two parts: trajectory flow matching and trajectory consistency. Through gradient analysis, we find that these terms are strongly negatively correlated, causing optimization conflict and slow convergence. Motivated by these insights, we introduce $Î±$-Flow, a broad family of objectives that unifies trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Model, and MeanFlow under one formulation. By adopting a curriculum strategy that smoothly anneals from trajectory flow matching to MeanFlow, $Î±$-Flow disentangles the conflicting objectives, and achieves better convergence. When trained from scratch on class-conditional ImageNet-1K 256x256 with vanilla DiT backbones, $Î±$-Flow consistently outperforms MeanFlow across scales and settings. Our largest $Î±$-Flow-XL/2+ model achieves new state-of-the-art results using vanilla DiT backbones, with FID scores of 2.58 (1-NFE) and 2.15 (2-NFE).
